failure_classification.explanation: glob-bracket.tests invokes the actual compiler from its generated loadables Makefile to create fnmatch and strmatch test programs. The compiler command was not found at line69, so the case aborted before any of its bracket-matching assertions. The driver then compared an empty output against glob-bracket.right and returned raw1. This is not evidence of a Bash glob implementation failure.

The unchanged 6856-assertion source did not finish within the declared900-second bound. One predeclared1800-second replay with the same CPU budget also timed out. Neither run printed the final assertion counts. This cannot honestly be assigned to a Bash semantic defect, a missing utility, or merely an insufficient timing assumption without further evidence. Both raw1460 outcomes and generation-accounting deficits remain explicit failures.

failure_classification.assumption: Two separate wall-clock samples remain within the same second
failure_classification.explanation: The sole diff is printf3.sub's own 'current time and -1 possible mismatch' warning. It compares an external date +%s sample with a subsequent Bash printf time=-1 sample for exact string equality. The recorded values are consecutive seconds, 11-Sep-2026 03:55:47 and 03:55:48. All other expected printf output matched. The raw1 failure is retained; no output or clock value was normalized and no retry was used to obtain a green second.

The unchanged read case timed out at900 seconds in read2.sub's loop of2001 timed FIFO reads. The retained output additionally proves that /dev/tty was unavailable to this noninteractive suite capture, a concrete terminal-prerequisite mismatch, but this does not prove the cause of the timeout. No observed assertion count establishes completion; do not reclassify the entire failure as harmless missingTTY or a known Bash defect.
